messages:
marta: Heads-up — I opened a draft TF change to make GPU pools account-scoped and to split KMS keys/IAM roles per billing-account. Planning conversation here before I raise the big PR.

raj: Can you paste the diff? curious what exactly triggers replacements.

marta: Sure — main points: move from a single shared aws_kms_key + shared iam role to per-account kms alias + iam role scoped by account_id. New var: `account_boundary_mode = \"per-account\" | \"global\"`.

marta: Terraform plan snippet from my sandbox:
```
-/+ aws_kms_key.gpu_key (new resource required)
  ~ resource "aws_iam_role" "gpu_service" will be replaced
  -/+ resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "attach_kms" will be replaced
```

chris: Oof, that will replace KMS keys (and re-encrypt). Any rekeying implications for existing volumes or secrets?

marta: Yes — KMS key replacement would trigger re-encryption for any resource using the key. Currently GPU node ebs volumes aren't encrypted with the key, but some S3 buckets and audit logs use it. I flagged a migration step to copy data/rotate aliases -> new key -> update references.

sofia: Let's not create a breaking global apply. Proposal: ship module v2 with the new behavior behind a feature flag boolean `enable_account_scoped_keys` default false. Then do a controlled migration per-account.

raj: Agreed. Also recommend a compatibility shim that creates the new alias but doesn't replace the old key until we run a state migration. Something like: create `aws_kms_alias.new_alias` pointing to `aws_kms_key.new` but don't reference it from resources until we run a `tf state mv` / replacement window.

marta: I prototyped that: create alias w/ lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } for the old key, and only flip references after `tf state replace-provider` & manual `state mv`. But we need an automated state migration plan in CI for the accounts we approve.

tom: On the IAM side, splitting roles per-account will force role re-creation. Is that required? Could we instead parameterize the role name to include account_id but keep `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` then create the new role and gradually update workloads to use it?

chris: We could also inline a fallback policy allowing both keys for a short window: new policy allows use of both old and new KMS keys so rolling nodes don't break. That buys time.

marta: Good call. I'll add a `dual_key_policy_enabled` flag and document a 72h window where both keys are valid.

sofia: Operational concerns: GitOps. We must avoid a large-scale diff where all clusters pick up v2 at once. How are we planning module pinning?

raj: Strategy: publish module v2.0.0. Update overlay repos for two canary clusters (account A: us-west-2-stage, account B: us-east-1-dev). Run full pipeline (plan -> apply) with extra verification. Only after signoff, update enterprise overlay batches.

marta: CI additions: terratest to validate that `terraform plan` for v2 with `enable_account_scoped_keys=false` yields no changes; then a separate job for `enable_account_scoped_keys=true` in canary accounts that exercises the migration script (dry-run). I added a `migrations/rename_kms_key.sh` (draft) that runs `terraform state mv` commands.

marta: migration script snippet:
```bash
# run in canary account workspace
terraform init -upgrade -backend-config=...
terraform plan -var='enable_account_scoped_keys=true' -out=plan.tfout
# inspect plan, then run state moves
terraform state mv module.gpu.aws_kms_key.gpu_key module.gpu.aws_kms_key.gpu_key_new
terraform apply plan.tfout
```

tom: Make sure to add a backup step: `aws s3 cp s3://tf-state/backup.tfstate s3://tf-state/backup-$(date +%s).tfstate` and snapshot any DBs.

chris: Also add a check to CI to detect any other infra depending on the KMS key (S3, CloudTrail, secrets). We should fail the canary plan if references exist and require manual thumbs-up.

sofia: From GitOps side, I can add a gating job that blocks the repo sync automation unless the plan file is signed off. We already have a `sync-blocker` annotation; will extend it to accept `kms-migration-approved` tag.

marta: Cost note: per-account keys will increase KMS monthly usage and key counts -> small bump. Also per-account IAM roles increase control plane entities. I estimated ~+$200/month for our top 20 accounts (KMS key charges). Adding that to the PR description.

raj: Capacity ops: if role/kms flip requires node restarts in worst-case, we need to reserve extra GPUs so scheduled workloads don't OOM. Can we do a warm reserve in the canary accounts?

marta: I spoke with capacity; they can temporarily add +10% GPU buffer in the canary accounts for 48h. We'll schedule the apply for off-peak.

ci-cd-bot: CI pipeline for branch `mod/v2-kms-account-boundary` failed: `terratest` step timeout (exit 1). Logs: `timed out waiting for test cluster`

marta: Will rerun after I fix the terratest cluster setup (forgot to set `GCP_REGION` override).

deploy-bot: FYI — an unrelated canary apply in `us-east-1` completed 12m ago (no conflicts).

marta: Next actions I will do: 1) open the formal PR with v2.0.0 and a migration playbook 2) add feature-flag default false, dual-key policy and lifecycle prevent_destroy shims 3) add terratest + state-migration job for canaries 4) coordinate reserve GPUs + schedule maintenance window.

sofia: I'll prepare the GitOps gating changes and the `kms-migration-approved` annotation.

raj: I'll review the PR and run security review for IAM/KMS policy changes.

chris: I can help write the policy that allows dual-key access safely and the re-encryption runbook.

marta: Thanks — I'll ping you all on the PR. If anyone sees a blocker, drop a note here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder — please file a post-change incident runbook entry in the `incidents` folder before starting canary apply.

marta: Filed: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042, added initial rollback steps.

tom: One more ask — include `terraform state list | grep kms` check in CI to enumerate all refs before migration. Prevents surprises.

marta: Good call, will add that to the CI preflight.

raj: Sounds like a solid plan. I'm marking this thread as the coordination hub; please @mention when the canary PR is ready.

marta: Will do. Thanks everyone!
